newsitem.title: FRANCE: Striking French rail men block Paris-Le Havre line.
newsitem.headline: Striking French rail men block Paris-Le Havre line.

text.p: Striking rail workers blocked the main railway line from Paris to the port of Le Havre in northwestern France on Wednesday in a protest over government plans to create a separate railtrack company.

The SNCF state railway company said strikers from three trade unions began blocking the Paris-Rouen-Le Havre line on Tuesday night after calling a 24-hour local stoppage at the depot of Sotteville-les-Rouen, starting point of last year's 24-day national rail strike.
The SNCF was diverting trains to Le Havre, causing delays of up to 90 minutes but few cancellations.
The local rail strike came on the 10th day of a strike by truck drivers which has increasingly choked roads in the French provinces and caused petrol shortages in several regions.

The disputes are not strictly related, but two major trade unions, the Communist-led CGT and the non-partisan Force Ouvriere, have called on members to support the truckers action to maximise pressure on the government and employers.
Pilots at state-owned Air France and Air France Europe began a two-day strike on Wednesday over their own working conditions, which the airlines said forced them to reduce services.

Air France was running two in three of its long-haul flights but only one-quarter of its European services. Air France Europe, its mainly domestic subsidiary, said it was running half of its normal schedule.
